KUALA LUMPUR: A potential electoral cooperation between Pakatan Harapan and Bersatu could strengthen both parties' prospects in the Melaka election by helping the coalition shore up Malay support and giving Bersatu a broader platform.

Political analysts said this could prevent a split in votes and enable PH and Bersatu to mount a stronger challenge against Barisan Nasional, which has emerged from recent state elections with strong results.

They said the biggest hurdle would be convincing PH grassroots to accept Bersatu, given the latter's role in the political upheaval that led to the collapse of the PH administration during the Sheraton Move in 2020.

Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said the proposed cooperation could give PH a stronger platform to challenge BN, particularly as PH continued to face difficulties in securing Malay support.

He said PH's performance in recent state elections highlighted the importance of bringing additional Malay support into any broader electoral arrangement, while Bersatu needed to work with a larger coalition to remain competitive.
"PH, after the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, found that it lacked Malay support.
"And Bersatu, after being sidelined by Pas, is on its own.
"Ber-satu cannot contest alone and needs to join a larger coalition."
BN won 48 of the 56 seats in the Johor election in July.
In the following month, it won 18 of the 36 seats in Negri Sembilan, with Perikatan Nasional taking seven.
Mazlan said Bersatu could provide PH with more support among Malay voters, while PH could give Bersatu a platform to remain electorally competitive.
He said this could be significant in mixed constituencies, where the combination of Malay and non-Malay support could allow PH and Bersatu to mount a stronger challenge.
"For Bersatu, there is no other option. BN will not accept it and Pas has already removed the party (from PN).
"What Bersatu has now is PH."
Mazlan said the proposed cooperation should not be viewed as unusual despite the history between the two parties.
"In politics, there are no permanent enemies and no permanent friends.
"What matters is how both parties can use the situation to strengthen their position."

International Islamic University Malaysia political analyst and Ishak Institute fellow Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said the proposed cooperation was realistic as PH and Bersatu were at a point where they had little to lose by exploring a new arrangement.
"But the problem is whether the grassroots, especially those in PH, can accept Bersatu, which is seen as having betrayed PH."
Syaza said the cooperation could make the contest more competitive by creating an almost one-to-one contest between the opposing sides, should BN and PN work together.
She said a split in votes between PH and Bersatu could make it easier for BN to secure victories, whereas cooperation could prevent opposition votes from being divided.
Syaza said the cooperation alone might not be enough for PH and Bersatu to secure 15 seats, the simple majority needed to form the government.
She said its immediate effect would instead be to make the contest more competitive.
The potential cooperation comes as the two sides continue discussions on a possible electoral arrangement for the election.

f8eb8e3a3107a65c: SANAA (Yemen), Oct 4 — In Yemen, coffee is more than a crop. It is part of the country’s history and identity, and growers and businesses are seeking to revive the industry amid years of conflict.
The effort was on display Thursday in Sanaa, where farmers, traders and coffee enthusiasts gathered to mark International Coffee Day.

“Coffee is a treasure for Yemen,” coffee farmer Sheikh Abed Rajeh told Xinhua at the event. Expanding the sector, he said, could raise incomes for rural communities and give a boost to Yemen’s economy.
Mohammed Al-Qasimi, head of the Coffee Unit at Sanaa’s agricultural authorities, said around 15 million coffee trees had been planted across the country over the past five years.

Yemen’s coffee production has risen from around 17,000 tonnes to between 42,000 and 45,000 tonnes in 2025, while output is expected to reach about 50,000 tonnes in 2026 as cultivation continues to expand, Al-Qasimi said.
An initiative is underway to plant 100 million coffee trees over 10 years, at a planned rate of 10 million trees a year, across Yemen’s mountains, slopes and agricultural terraces, he added.
For Yemen, the effort is about more than increasing production. It is also an attempt to reclaim a centuries-old place in global coffee history.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Yemenis tour a coffee fair in the capital Sanaa on September 30, 2022, on the eve of the International Coffee Day. — AFP
Coffee grown in Yemen’s highlands was once shipped through the Red Sea port of Mocha to overseas markets, eventually giving the port’s name to one of the world’s most familiar coffee terms.

Al-Qasimi estimated that around 250,000 people work across the coffee sector, including farmers, intermediaries and traders, while more than 276 companies, projects and entrepreneurs have entered the industry in recent years.
Yemeni coffee is now sold in Gulf countries, the United States, Europe and Asia, with producers looking to expand into more international markets.

“We are trying to bring Yemeni coffee back to local and international markets,” said Ghaleb Al-Emadi, owner of the Haraz Coffee Centre. The centre has worked since 2016 to promote the identity and distinctive flavor of Yemeni coffee internationally, he said.
Producers are also seeking to capitalise on the premium reputation of Yemeni beans.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A speciality coffee shop employee serves filtered coffee at the shop in Yemen's Houthi-held capital Sanaa on July 18, 2023. — AFP pic
At a national coffee auction, a kilogramme of coffee sold for as much as US$976 (RM3,986), Al-Qasimi said, underscoring the value that exceptional Yemeni varieties can command.
But getting that coffee to overseas buyers remains a major challenge.
Years of conflict in Yemen have disrupted roads, ports and trade routes, and driven up transportation costs, making it harder for coffee producers to connect directly with international markets.
Al-Qasimi said the cost of sending a one-kilogramme coffee sample overseas has risen from around US$20 to as much as US$120, while delivery times have increased dramatically.
A sample that once reached an overseas customer within three days can now take between 20 and 30 days. Larger shipments that previously arrived within a week can now take three to four months.
“The demand is there. The difficult part is getting our coffee to the customer,” Al-Qasimi said. — Bernama-Xinhua
b3610fa770a4c19e: MEXICO CITY, Oct 4 — Lawyers and environmentalists from Latin America unveiled a model law this week that punishes severe environmental harm by eliminating excuses for failing to protect ecosystems, one of its authors told AFP.
Latin America is home to about a third of the world’s biodiversity.
It is also one of the most dangerous regions for environmental defenders, with dozens murdered each year.
The region also suffers from high rates of impunity for environmental crimes, or “ecocide,” a term used to describe serious harm against the natural world.
“We are champions at passing beautiful laws that are then not enforced,” Rodrigo Lledo, Latin America director of the organisation Stop Ecocide International, told AFP by telephone.
The Model Ecocide Law was presented Thursday in Mexico City by Stop Ecocide along with the Mexican centre for environmental justice CEMDA and researchers at Mexico’s Iberoamericana University.
It gives Latin American congresses a framework to “penalise serious environmental destruction,” Stop Ecocide said in a statement.
The mock law calls for governments to give greater protection, such as a police escort, to whistleblowers, witnesses and experts in criminal cases of ecocide.
It also proposes harsher penalties for crimes committed against them, in order to “prevent and, eventually, punish those who want to attack those who protect nature,” Lledo added.
According to the NGO Global Witness, 85 per cent of the 124 murders of environmental activists in 2025 took place in Latin America.
Attempts by local jurisdictions to boost environmental protections have been hobbled by a lack of enforcement.

A decade after the Constitutional Court of Colombia declared the Atrato River a “living entity” with “rights” to protection and conservation, the waterway continues to be affected by pollution caused by illegal mining.

The Model Ecocide Law argues that the difficulty in identifying the perpetrators of environmental crimes does not exempt the state from its responsibility to stop the destruction and repair the damage.
It aims to push governments to effectively pursue those responsible and prevent prosecutors from simply halting investigations because of the difficulty in finding the culprits.
“There is no excuse,” Lledo said. “This is the underlying philosophy.” — AFP
dc49b66c985dfde8: MOSCOW, Oct 4 — Russia plans to sharply increase defence spending, cut funding for education and raise taxes next year as costs mount in its war with Ukraine, draft budget documents show.
The budget comes as the Ukraine war grinds through its fifth year, with both sides intensifying long-range strikes and Moscow pummelling Kyiv in daily air attacks.
Here’s what we know about the plans, which have been submitted to Russia’s lower house of parliament for approval:
Defence spending to soar

The government plans to spend a record 17.1 trillion rubles (US$204 billion; RM833.1 billion) on defence in 2027, around 26 per cent higher than last year’s forecast for 2027, according to the draft budget.
Defence spending will account for more than a third of all outlays and will be higher than spending earmarked for healthcare, education and social welfare combined, the documents show.
While the documents forecast defence spending will decrease in 2028 and 2029, Russia has repeatedly overshot long-term defence spending forecasts since launching its Ukraine offensive.
Actual spending on defence is classified and could rise even further, said Alexander Kolyandr, a senior fellow at the Center for European Policy Analysis.
“The published totals are merely an opening bid in the negotiation between the finance ministry and the security establishment,” he said in an article last week.
Social spending squeezed
Unveiling the draft budget last week, Russia’s finance minister Anton Siluanov described both funding for social welfare and defence spending as a “priority”.
But the budget documents show big cuts in non-military sectors, including social policy.

Planned outgoings on healthcare and education are set to drop by more than five per cent each compared with original plans for 2027, while funding on social programmes are set to plunge by more than six per cent.
Among the planned cuts are the federal government’s anti-cancer programme, which is set to lose around 97 per cent of its original budgeted funding, the documents show.

“The government is cutting back on civil servant pay and reducing their numbers, while slashing infrastructure projects, including construction and roadwork,” columnist Boris Grozovsky said in an article for the Important Stories media outlet on Tuesday.
To cover the shortfall, the government has proposed tax hikes, among them higher rates on bank deposits and property sales.
Debt is up
Russia has clocked a deficit each year since launching its Ukraine offensive.

Total shortfalls are estimated to be around 5.4 trillion rubles (US$64.4 billion; RM263 billion) in 2027, more than 70 per cent per cent higher than the 3.2 trillion ruble deficit for 2027 forecast last year.
State debt is set to rise above 20 per cent of GDP in 2027, which is low for international standards but above the level Russia’s finance ministry had previously described as “safe”.
And total government borrowing in 2027 is estimated to be about 43 per cent more than had been originally planned last year.
“There’s not enough money,” Grozovsky said.
“The government is sending a signal to everyone: don’t count on budget funds: they’ll go to those who absolutely must be given them.” — AFP
fb8f4282780d419f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Universiti Malaya (UM), through its Academy of Malay Studies (APM), is organising a Typewriter Exhibition of a diverse collection as an effort to appreciate the historical heritage and evolution of writing and communication technology.

In a statement today, UM said the exhibition, held from September 1 to October 31 at the Malay Ethnographic Museum, features more than 50 typewriters from museums, galleries, libraries and local collectors.

According to the statement, the exhibition showcases a variety of typewriter designs, brands and models, as well as several special segments, including the Figure Collection, Multiscript Typewriters and Jawi Typewriter Heritage.

78da2c27a68d2460: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Gone are the days of traditional cinema where it was just about watching movies as audiences today crave more exciting shared experiences.

This change, which can be considered a result of an eventful past six years that included the rise of over-the-top (OTT) platforms coupled with the Covid-19 Pandemic that almost crippled the cinema sector, has also reshaped how audiences view cinemas today.
According to GSC Chief Executive Officer Koh Mei Lee, while audience footfall has shown encouraging signs of recovery, attendance still lags behind pre-pandemic levels by roughly 20 per cent.

“Consumer behaviour has since evolved, with audiences becoming more discerning about entertainment experiences, showing greater demand for premium, immersive and event-driven experiences in cinemas,” Koh said.

GSC is currently Malaysia’s biggest cinema chain operator with a total of 505 screens across 53 locations nationwide, including four ultra-premium ‘Luxe’ locations under its flagship Aurum Theatre and Velvet Cinemas sub-brands.
In an interview with Malay Mail, Koh dived deeper into how they had to revisit the drawing board for their offerings to satisfy this new and growing demand along with other factors leading to it.
Expanding beyond traditional means

In response to the changing landscape of cinema, GSC has expanded its offerings beyond the screen, now shifting to more fan-centric events such as special screenings, concert films, and live viewing parties that come with interactive activities, and of course, freebies.

This can be seen through some of their recent events such as ScareFest 2026, which united horror film enthusiasts with special screenings past midnight, as well as the Football Final Live Viewing Party in conjunction with the recent Fifa World Cup Finals.
They have also introduced out-of-the-box events such as the 24-hour Spider-Man: Brand New Day Marathon, where they offered special showtime slots until 6am.
Their recent Winefest 2026, which focused on food, beverage and lifestyle enthusiasts also demonstrated the versatility of their cinema and dining spaces.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
GSC’s ScareFest 2026 united horror film fans with special screenings past midnight and some ‘uninvited’ guests. — Picture courtesy of GSC

On top of that, GSC has also invested more in premium large-format screens such as IMAX, 4DX and ScreenX to meet current demand. The latest examples can be seen through the introduction of IMAX with Laser halls at GSC Paradigm in Johor as well as in IOI Mall Damansara.
“Audience preferences are constantly evolving, and we see that as an opportunity to redefine what the cinema experience can be.
“Audiences still love watching great movies on the big screen, but they’re also seeking additional social and memorable experiences.

“GSC connects storytelling, technology, lifestyle, community — uniting film, F&B, events and digital experiences all under one brand, and as such we have expanded beyond just traditional movie screenings,” Koh said.

She also said that these experiences actually complement movies even more instead of replacing them, adding that their goal is to keep pushing the boundaries of cinema by creating total entertainment experiences while preserving the magic of the big screens.
Veiled challenges
Koh pointed out that running a cinema chain is not an easy feat and more often than not, its challenges are often overlooked especially when it comes to operating costs.

She shared that operating cinemas involves high fixed overheads — such as technology maintenance, utilities, and staffing — making operational efficiency essential even as attendance lags behind pre-pandemic levels.

This is why policy relief has proven vital, as demonstrated by the government’s decision to reduce the Entertainment Duty in the Federal Territory from 25 per cent to 10 per cent in 2024, which will be in effect until December 2028.

“Box office revenue and cinema screens grew by three per cent and 30 per cent, respectively, contrasting with the broader national trend, which noted declines of 18 per cent in box office revenues and 32 per cent in the number of cinema screens,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
GSC chief executive officer Koh Mei Lee. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin

Koh, who is also part of the local coalition Industry Unite, which is calling for the abolishment of the Entertainments Duty Act 1953, reiterated the importance of its abolishment for the future of the local cinema industry.

“The relief would enable cinema operators like GSC to continue investing in cinema infrastructure, particularly in modernising older locations and upgrading digital technologies across locations to meet the growing demand for premium large-format experiences.
“And also to strengthen the operational resilience of cinemas in an increasingly competitive entertainment landscape,” she said.
Koh also revealed that the growth of OTT or streaming platforms has changed audience behaviour when it comes to opting for cinemas as an entertainment option.
She said that audiences would reserve cinema visits only for major blockbuster and premium large-formats releases such as Obsession, Michael, Toy Story 5, The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
“This makes it increasingly important for GSC to create experiences that cannot be replicated through home entertainment,” she said.
Moving forward

Despite the shifting landscape and veiled challenges, there are still some positive takeaways according to Koh, which include the growing appetite for cinema experiences that extend beyond the ‘movie-verse’.
“We have seen stronger interest in complementary experiences such as themed food and beverage offerings, limited-edition merchandise, fan-centric events, and community gatherings.

“These allow audiences to celebrate their favourite movies together with like-minded fans — creating shared moments and immersive experiences that can only truly come to life within the cinema,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A shot from GSC’s live viewing party of the recent Fifa World Cup Final. — Picture courtesy of GSC

Further supplementing this trend, GSC also offers movie-goers several incentives via their GSC Rewards membership programme and promotions that encourage repeat visits while rewarding movie-goers’ loyalty.

Koh also shared that admissions during the first half of 2025 benefited from a strong line-up of local and Hollywood releases, such as Ne Zha 2, Blood Brothers, Ejen Ali 2 and Captain America: Brave New World.
While the release calendar this year has been more varied, they are expecting a better second half for 2026 with a strong lineup of upcoming blockbusters such as Dune: Part 3 and Avengers: Doomsday.
410fa479d53aca11: RIJEKA, Croatia: Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka both struck twice as England ran riot in a 7-0 rout of abject Croatia in the Nations League on Saturday.
Thomas Tuchel's side ripped Croatia to shreds in Rijeka to make it two wins from their first three matches in their Nations League group.
England captain Kane's double extended his record goal tally for his country to 89.
But the Bayern Munich striker was far from the only stand-out performer for England.
Arsenal winger Saka also bagged a brace as England recorded the biggest win of the Tuchel era.
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham, restored to the starting line-up after Tuesday's 2-0 win against Czech Republic, was on target to cap a vibrant display featuring three assists.
The effervescent Anthony Gordon netted to make it four goals in his last four England matches before Morgan Rogers completed the annihilation.
Chasing a top-two finish to secure a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals in March, England conclude the international break against Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday.
That should be a slightly more raucous occasion than this tie, which was played 'behind closed doors' because of crowd trouble involving Croatia fans against France in 2025.
Around 6,000 local school children and 100 England supporters were allowed into the Stadion HNK Rijeka, creating a subdued environment in a country known for its hostile atmospheres.
England's players had taken a dip in the nearby Adriatic Sea earlier in the week, prompting Tuchel to warn the relaxed mood in the camp must not put his team into "holiday mode."
But with the Adriatic shimmering in the sun just yards from the stadium, it was child's play for England as they demolished ageing Croatia to disappoint the youthful crowd.
Tuchel's men took just eight minutes to go ahead with an incisive raid that exposed the talent gap between the side.
Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, making his first start for England, was the catalyst with a composed pass to Bellingham.
Bellingham slipped an equally measured ball in behind the flat-footed Croatia defence and Kane took a deft touch before stroking a clinical finish into the roof of the net from 10 yards.
No mercy
England had too much pace and poise for Croatia and it was no surprise when Bellingham increased their advantage at the end of flowing 27-pass move in the 21st minute.
Saka's cross was too high for his team-mates, but Gordon adroitly controlled the ball in mid-air and whipped it back into the six-yard box, where Bellingham stretched to poke into the far corner.
Gordon put the result beyond doubt in the 39th minute, diving to meet Jarell Quansah's pin-point cross with an agile header that flashed past Dominik Livakovic from six yards.

Quansah's assist was a timely riposte to the critics who said Tuchel was wrong to select him instead of Trent Alexander-Arnold after the Real Madrid right-back made his first England start in nearly two years against Czech Republic.
England beat Croatia 4-2 in June in their opening World Cup group game, but this was a far more one-sided encounter.

Bellingham was in irrepressible mood, driving into the Croatia area and baffling Luka Modric with a smooth drag-back before crossing low towards Saka, who slotted home from close-range on the stroke of half-time.
England showed no mercy after the interval and Kane netted again in the 53rd minute, sliding in to convert Anderson's cross with ease.
Saka got the sixth from Kane's pass after another woeful error from hapless Croatia in the 68th minute.
Rogers came off the bench to put the seal on England's swaggering display, rounding Livakovic to net from Bellingham's 87th minute pass.

af35aab989dec3fa: LIMA: Scientists have discovered a new species of lizard in the Peruvian Andes, the Natural History Museum of San Marcos University said Saturday.
The lizard measures between six and eight centimeters and has distinct coloration depending on sex.
Females have square-shaped spots on their backs, while males have oblique spots and white scales that help them blend into their rocky surroundings.
The lizard feeds on plants and small arthropods, including spiders, beetles, true bugs and insect larvae.
The new species was found at an altitude of more than 4,800m in the southern Andean region of Arequipa and was given the name Liolaemus archipensis.
"The description of a new species represents a very important advance for biodiversity in our country," biologist Ling Huamani-Valderrama, who led the research, told AFP.
Peru is home to 296 species of lizard, according to the biologist. The discovery was published in the Swiss scientific journal Diversity.
5a8589595e9016a2: BEIJING: World No.1 Elena Rybakina could not regroup and fell to 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva in the second round of the China Open on Saturday in Beijing.
The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan was playing her first match since seizing the top ranking on her US Open win in New York, but Armenia's Charaeva triumphed 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in a clinical comeback.
"I don't have words," said Charaeva, who is making her Beijing debut.
"She's (an) amazing player, and for me it's kind of just dream come true," she said of Rybakina.
"I will be really happy to stay some more days in Beijing," she added. "Never stop believing, I guess."
Rybakina got off to a solid start, but seven double-faults ushered the momentum into the hands of her opponent.
Wind rattled the closed-roof stadium, with both players serving as thunderous claps echoed over the court.
A supportive crowd tried to rally Rybakina back into contention, but Charaeva held serve to win the match in two hours and 11 minutes.
Charaeva faces Briton Sonay Kartal in the third round.
c16170fb61d1776e: DUBAI: Iran's rial continued its decline on Saturday, as the central bank announced an injection of up to US$2 billion to support the currency while the economy faces US sanctions and a naval blockade.

The US dollar was sold for around 2.688 million rials, up from 2.632 million on Friday, according to free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, while alanchand.com reported 2.695 million rials per dollar.
State television said state banks began selling up to US$2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value in the past year.

With an inflation rate of more than 70%, life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent ​as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline -- oil exports.
Many Iranians seeking safe havens for their savings have been buying dollars, other hard currencies or gold.

Mehdi Darabi, an aide to the central bank's governor on foreign exchange affairs, blamed the decline of the rial partly on what he said were false predictions by US officials of the collapse of the Iranian economy.

"It is suggested that the Iranian economy is about to crash... The enemy is using this to affect the exchange rate of our currency," Darabi told state TV, adding that the current fall of the rial was temporary.

446d7413491c8dcc: PETALING JAYA: Seorang pelajar perempuan berusia 16 tahun ditemui meninggal dunia di sebuah sekolah menengah di Yong Peng di Batu Pahat, Johor petang semalam.

Pelajar Tingkatan Empat itu dilaporkan ditemui neneknya yang datang ke sekolah selepas menyedari cucunya tidak pulang ke rumah kira-kira 5.30 petang selepas menghadiri kelas bimbangan, lapor Harian Metro.
Difahamkan, pelajar itu ditemui dalam keadaan terbaring dan lemah di kawasan dewan sekolah selain terdapat kesan darah kering pada badan mangsa.

Sementara itu, Timbalan Ketua Polis Johor, Hoo Chuan Huat meminta orang ramai dan pihak media memberi ruang kepada pihak berkuasa untuk menjalankan siasatan menyeluruh mengenai kematian pelajar berkenaan.
Katanya, polis masih dalam proses mengumpulkan fakta serta maklumat tepat berhubung kejadian itu dan terlalu awal untuk mengesahkan sebarang spekulasi yang sedang berlegar.
"Kita masih dalam proses dapatkan maklumat tersebut. Macam pemberita juga kena dapatkan maklumat. Saya tak boleh bercakap betul ke tak betul sebab kami masih dapatkan maklumat.

"Saya tak mengesahkan apa benda sebab kami sedang dapatkan maklumat. Terlampau awal untuk mengesahkan suatu kes kalau tak dapat satu. Kami sedang dapatkan maklumat. Bagi peluang kepada kami untuk jalankan siasatan," katanya yang dipetik Astro Awani sebagai berkata.
f1fc79b098da3aba: OVIEDO, Spain: Lamine Yamal continued his superb goalscoring form as Spain secured a 3-1 win over the Czech Republic on Saturday in the Nations League.
The world champions moved three points clear of England at the top of Group A3, after Thomas Tuchel's side demolished Croatia 7-0 earlier on in Rijeka.
Spain cruised into a two-goal lead with Yamal and Rodri Hernandez on target but Jiri Slama gave the Czechs a chance by pulling one back with 20 minutes to go.

However Mikel Merino wrapped up Spain's win late on after Ladislav Krejci was sent off for the Czechs as Spain racked up a 41st consecutive unbeaten game, including the World Cup final win over Argentina in July.
Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made several changes in Oviedo from Tuesday's win over Croatia, including handing debuts to full-back Ivan Fresneda and striker Roberto Fernandez.
It was one of Spain's star names, though, who lit up the game early on, something he is beginning to make a habit of.
Yamal, who scored in the second minute of Spain's first two games against England and Croatia, waited as long as the sixth before breaking the deadlock.
The 19-year-old winger, a major candidate for the Ballon d'Or, produced an exquisite finish from the right of the box, curled into the top corner after taking a touch to earn himself room to shoot.
Spain coach De la Fuente put his hands to his head in apparent shock at the quality of Yamal's superb strike. It was the youngster's 11th goal in his last eight games for club and country.
The winger's Barcelona team-mate Rodri doubled Spain's lead after 35 minutes, arriving in the box to drill into the top corner after the ball fell nicely for him.
De la Fuente took off Yamal at half-time to give the young Barcelona star a break before Tuesday's visit to face Croatia.
With the teenager no longer gracing the Carlos Tartiere pitch the pace of the game slowed in the second half.
The Czechs pulled one back through Slama, who produced an excellent low finish across David Raya after Adam Hlozek played him in.
Arsenal stopper Raya was fortunate a few minutes later when he conceded possession with a misplaced pass while out of his goal, but the visitors could not capitalise.
Raya also spilled the ball badly and Ryan Naderi turned home but the goal was disallowed for a foul on Robin Le Normand.
Czech Republic's determined efforts to battle back were derailed by Krejci's red card, with the defender shown a second yellow for pulling back Fernandez.
Liverpool winger Victor Munoz prodded wide before Merino rounded off the win in the final stages with a finish from close range.

a977bb4d8841eec4: NEW YORK: Indian police on Saturday detained dozens of youth protesters in New Delhi on the second straight day of demonstrations demanding the chief election commissioner's resignation over alleged voter-roll irregularities.

The demonstrations have been backed by key opposition parties, including the popular Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), who say voter-roll changes give an advantage to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.
There was a heavy police presence around Jantar Mantar, a government-designated protest site in the heart of New Delhi, which remained sealed off behind police barricades.
Local media reports said more than 100 protesters demanding that Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down were detained.
"Delhi Police must stop its crackdown on protesting students and activists," CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post.
"Every attempt to suppress peaceful protesters will only bring more people to the streets and strengthen the march to Jantar Mantar," Dipke added.
"Dissent is a democratic right. It cannot be crushed through intimidation or force".
Delhi police did not comment on the reported detentions but warned that "unauthorised gatherings", processions and demonstrations were prohibited around Jantar Mantar.
"No permission has been granted for any protest scheduled for today... nor has any prior intimation regarding any such protest been received by New Delhi District Police," police said.
Anti-government activist Yogendra Yadav said: "If a designated protest site cannot accommodate peaceful dissent, where does democracy leave room for protest?"
'Peaceful dissent'

e702ddd06989d09e: MADRID: Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities in Spain on Saturday to demand affordable housing, a day after lawmakers rejected relief measures for tenants.
The demonstrations extended a crisis that has gone on for more than a week, triggered by the eviction last month of a pensioner, 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, from her Madrid flat.

The defeat was another political setback for Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and has renewed questions over whether his minority government can survive until the next scheduled general election in 2027.

His government's proposed measures, which included automatic renewal of tenancy contracts and restrictions on evicting vulnerable tenants, were voted down by opposition parties on Friday in Spain's parliament.
The defeat infuriated those protesting the country's increasingly expensive housing market.
Hundreds of protesters have been occupying a tent city set up a week ago in the heart of Madrid to press for reforms.
Late on Saturday groups of far-right protesters, some of them performing Nazi salutes, tried to get to the camp but were blocked by police.
One video posted on the website of Spanish daily El Pais showed police chasing some members of the group through the streets and the newspaper also reported that officers had made three arrests.
General strike call
Earlier Saturday, demonstrators marched through the capital's streets. Authorities said 70,000 people participated, but the organisers put the figure at 500,000.
Smaller demonstrations took place in other cities, including Palma de Mallorca, Santander, Segovia and Toledo. In Valencia, five people were arrested after clashes with police, local media reported.

At the Madrid protest Marcos Sainz, a librarian of 26, said he used to rent a two-bedroom apartment with friends for a total monthly rent of 900 euros. Today, a one-bedroom flat often costs 1,000 euros -- or half the median monthly salary in the capital, he told AFP.
He would protest rental spikes "until someone dares to regulate it all as (otherwise) we'll all have to leave Madrid and that would be a shame as I am from Madrid".
"We are demanding a fundamental right," said Javier, a 31-year-old solar panel installer. "Decent housing, stability and conditions allowing us to construct a decent life project.
"I spend half of my salary on a tiny room," he added.
Valeria Racu, one of the spokesmen of the Tenants' Union organising the protest, said in a statement that the last eight days' protests had shown the effectiveness of people's power.
"Now begins real politics -- politics which has always belonged to the people and which will return once and for all to the streets," she added.
She repeated her union's call for a general strike.
Calls for early election
Housing has for years been a top concern for Spaniards as supply falls short of demand, with rents and house prices rising as elsewhere in the EU.
Average rents in Spain have almost doubled over the past decade, while asking prices for homes have risen by about 90%, according to real estate website Idealista.
Abascal's eviction catalysed long-running anger about runaway housing costs.

The pensioner was forced to leave the Madrid flat where she had lived for more than seven decades after it was acquired by an investment company that sought to increase her rent by 275%, say housing campaigners.
The backlash led the property's new owners to reach a deal allowing her to return to the flat at a low rent.

The housing bills Sanchez's leftist coalition had presented to parliament were rejected after the Catalan separatist party Junts -- on whose support the government relies -- voted against them, arguing they lacked rigour.
Junts joined the main opposition Popular Party (PP) and the far-right Vox party in shooting down the measures.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo on Saturday urged Sanchez to call early elections "because the country can't take any more".
Recent opinion polls have generally placed the Popular Party ahead of the Socialists.
7c3e0b60a0264442: NEW YORK: Another former OpenAI employee has added his voice to a chorus of frantic calls to make AI safe, saying the industry must mimic the aviation or nuclear power sectors with their layers of safeguards to avoid disaster.

In an article published in The Atlantic Magazine, David Robinson echoed warnings from inside and outside the AI world that its agents are being developed so fast and becoming so smart they could soon elude control and conceivably wipe out humanity.

Robinson said alarming incidents reported since the start of the summer -- in which AI agents slipped out of their controlled spaces and went rogue to attack a variety of targets -- show the industry is not taking safety nearly seriously enough as it sprints to develop faster and more powerful artificial intelligence capabilities.
In the essay Robinson said his credentials include overseeing the writing of safety reports on 12 advanced model product launches and leading the drafting of OpenAI's Preparedness Framework.
Robinson says he worked at OpenAI for three-and-a-half years and was among the longest-tenured employees at the company.
The mistakes revealed recently are typical because of "the speed and flexibility with which people operate," Robinson wrote.
He added: "An environment where things like this can happen is no place to grow artificial minds that could be smarter than we are and that might not do what we want them to."

He argued that cutting-edge AI labs need to operate like the aviation or the nuclear industry with layers of redundant safeguards and careful planning "so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster."

Robinson also insisted that the issue of "alignment" -- the industry term for how AI can be trained to respect human values -- is essential but something the industry has failed to even define, much less master.
Then there's this, he said: AI models are getting better and better at detecting when they are being tested and might behave differently when they are actually deployed, fooling their masters.

After a meeting Tuesday at the White House, amid global worries about what AI means for humanity, top AI executives said they had committed to measures for self-regulation, as opposed to submitting to government rules. This includes internal controls on AI systems and bringing in outside analysts.
President Donald Trump is vehemently against government regulation of AI and insists that criticism that AI is dangerous is just a "hoax".

3d36fedd0ac8bcd8: KUALA LUMPUR: Steven Gerrard rolled back the years with a stunning hat-trick, scoring with the final kick of the match to seal a 7-6 victory for AllStar Premier Legends over AllStar World Legends at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) on Saturday.

7678b43e0eb35767: WHEN Jenette Torres Odena's 3-year-old son fell ill days after receiving a jab as part of a Philippine vaccination drive, his photograph spread on Facebook alongside claims the inoculation had killed him.

Doctors found no link between the boy's condition and the measles-rubella vaccine, and he went on to fully recover, but by then his image had appeared in anti-vaccine videos viewed hundreds of thousands of times.
"I felt like crying," Odena said. "I kept praying for my son to recover, and suddenly, they were killing him on Facebook."
The videos were part of a wave of misinformation that accompanied a child vaccination campaign this year that saw more than seven million Filipinos inoculated. Some 230,000 declined the jab.
The Department of Health said concerns about side effects accounted for 66 per cent of refusals and called misinformation spread by social media influencers a "major driver" of vaccine fear.
The Philippines has struggled to restore routine childhood immunisation rates after years of plummeting coverage, which contributed to a polio resurgence in 2019 and recurring measles outbreaks.

The claims circulated on social media recycled conspiracy theories that gained traction during the Covid-19 pandemic while tapping into lingering fears about vaccine safety after the botched rollout of a dengue vaccine in the Philippines a decade ago.

"Vaccine hesitancy should not simply be understood as a lack of scientific knowledge among the public," saod Daniel Fritz Silvallana, a health communication researcher at Deakin University, Australia.
"In the Philippine context, it is also connected to questions of trust, politics and people's previous experiences with vaccination and public health institutions."

Within days of the photo of Odena's son being shared online, Facebook content creator Maharani Sona Shiloh had incorporated it into a video, framing it as evidence the vaccination campaign was harming children.
To bolster her claims, Shiloh cited Trump's recent controversial move to reduce the number of vaccine doses administered to American children.
The video viewed hundreds of thousands of times paired the child's image with a photograph of US President Donald Trump and the words "Everyday slaughter".
Facebook eventually took down the page. Three affiliated pages remain active.
Shiloh rejected suggestions she was spreading harmful misinformation, describing herself as a human rights advocate.

The 44-year-old said she became involved in anti-vaccine advocacy years before the pandemic, later connecting with church groups and "advocacy circles" that also campaign against SIM card registration and other policies they associate with a treacherous "New World Order".

Videos posted by Shiloh, some with millions of views, claimed vaccines contained harmful substances, including "human placenta" and "formalin", while warning that the World Health Organisation was trying to depopulate the planet.
One mother, who asked to speak anonymously to protect her children, said she decided to hold off on vaccinating them after watching the videos.
A week after the Facebook page was shuttered, she said she remained undecided about vaccinating her children, explaining that she and her husband worried about possible side effects.
While Shiloh's claims quickly collapse under scientific scrutiny, vaccinologist Helen Petousis-Harris of the University of Auckland said these videos rely on fear rather than compelling evidence.
"Recognised vaccine ingredients become mysterious contaminants. Rare adverse events become brain damage, epilepsy organ failure and death."
For health workers on the frontlines, however, the videos are increasingly difficult to ignore.
"They get scared because the vlog said vaccines are fatal," said Wenna Mae Belen, a rural health worker in Sorsogon province.
"They tell me if something bad happens, they'll make me suck the vaccines out of their kids' bodies."
While Facebook bore "major responsibility" for the spread of vaccine misinformation, she said picking fights with content creators like Shiloh and their followers was a losing battle.
Rebuilding trust will take time and patience, she said, calling for open, non-judgmental conversations with parents.

47d28e64969c8278: AS America's military cyberdefence professionals met for their annual trade meeting in Maryland last Thursday, top commanders issued a blunt warning that sustained operations this year had cost the United States much of its long-built-up advantages in cyberspace.

According to US officials, highly sophisticated cyberattacks were at the heart of operations earlier this year, firstly to capture Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and then to degrade Iranian sensors and communications in the US-led Operation Epic Fury.

Over time, however, senior officials told the gathering of the Military Cyber Professionals Association, known as Hammercon, their ability to conduct offensive cyberattacks through pre-identified vulnerabilities in hostile systems has begun eroding fast.

"Your cyber magazine of these exquisite fires is empty pretty damn quick," Vice-Admiral Heidi Berg, commander of the US Navy Fleet Cyber Command, said in response to a question, referring to the abilities to hack and frustrate or turn off key systems in an opposing nation.

According to Lieutenant-General Christopher Eubank, head of US Army Cyber Command speaking at the same event, demand for direct US cyber support to wider military operations had been "constant" since the conflict with Iran began on Feb 28.
He said this was the "first time for the cyber force at large" that operations have been at such a tempo.
Those lessons in cyberspace appear to overlap heavily with much wider trend, particularly the overuse of precision missiles, including those for air defence.

Multiple US military sources told Reuters the Pentagon had used up large stockpiles of ATACMS strike missiles, Patriot air defence systems and Tomahawk long-range cruise missiles, to the point that it would take multiple years to rebuild "magazine depth".
The strain has also been telling on other parts of the US military.

Last week, US Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier had attempted suicide during its unusually long 286 consecutive days at sea this year supporting operations in the Middle East.
Events this year have acted as a savage and robust reminder of US military strength.
They have shown the stark limits of that power and the damage to the US military inventory goes well beyond just the used up missile stocks.

According to US specialist defence media reports, the US Air Force has lost as many as 40 of its MQ-9 Reaper drones in its operations since the end of February, as much as a quarter of its total airworthy fleet.

Other aircraft losses have also been on a scale unseen in recent US wars, including two KC-135 tankers destroyed and another seven damaged, a wrecked E-3 Sentry airborne warning aircraft, four destroyed F-15E Strike Eagles and another eight damaged.
Two MC-130J gunships and an A-10 Warthog were also lost on a mission to retrieve a downed pilot.

Still, estimates from the Congressional Budget Office put the financial expense of Operation Epic Fury so far as just under US$40 billion, pointedly warning it would take several years to rebuild depleted stocks of interceptor missiles critical for deterring any future war with China.
This week, US military publication Stars and Stripes noted that the US was moving to store long-range Typhon and High Mobility Artillery Rocket System missiles at Kadena Air Force Base in Okinawa.

That move was announced jointly with Japan and likely intended to reassure US regional allies and remind Beijing that, despite a largely friendly meeting between US President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping, the US remains ready to fight a war if needed.

When it comes to supporting allies this year, the US record has been distinctly mixed — with Saudi Arabia, in particular, now turning to wider foreign help despite the presence of what Gulf media say have been more than 100 US advisers on the ground.

According to French President Emmanuel Macron, French troops and missiles are now helping protect the Saudi port of Yanbu, while Riyadh is publicly discussing further support with treaty allies Pakistan and Turkiye.
Russian missiles, meanwhile, continue to pound Ukrainian targets, now helped by a lack of US-manufactured interceptors.
A broader realisation is that launching conflict is much easier to do than managing the resulting fallout.
The writer is from Reuters

2e403cdd5edafbc9: THE revelation that Zetrix AI Bhd, formerly known as MyEG Sdn Bhd, owes the Road Transport Department (RTD) more than RM200 million in unremitted collections is shocking.
The e-government services pioneer, which has operated since 2000, collected payments on behalf of the Road Transport Department (RTD) for road tax, driving licences and traffic summonses.

Zetrix, which assumed its new name in July last year 2025, reportedly failed to remit the fees it collected from the start of its three-year contract in May 2023. Why did Zetrix stop remitting the money? We do not know, but its financial position raises questions.

Corporate disclosures and media reports show that its development expenditure rose sharply to more than RM3.7 billion, while it also faced substantial debt obligations. Still, motorists have not been left without options, as RTD JPJ has directed them to its official and alternative payment channels.

Now comes the crunch. The Zetrix issue raises serious questions about RTD's financial controls, monitoring and accountability. It is no longer just about the money, but how the situation was allowed to persist without earlier intervention.
The obvious questions are: what safeguards were in place and, if they existed, why did they fail?
What were Zetrix's contractual obligations for remitting the collections? Are collections reconciled daily, weekly or monthly with RTD's records?
Are there automatic alerts when payments are overdue, independent audits and clear escalation procedures?
Were there earlier warnings, discrepancies, demands for payment or breaches of contractual obligations? If there were warnings, why was stronger action not taken earlier?

Agencies that appoint private firms to collect funds on behalf of the government must have robust systems to ensure prompt and accurate remittance. If such controls existed, RTD has some explaining to do: Why was there a lapse in compliance?, AND Why were the arrears allowed to accumulate?

Accountability must extend beyond recovering the more than RM200 million. The government needs to establish exactly how the arrears were allowed to build up, whether existing monitoring systems failed, and what safeguards are needed to prevent a similar situation involving public collections from happening again.

10cb2647cf5631e8: The second Anthropic-linked vulnerability known to have been exploited in the wild saw initial activity from an IP address in China targeting vulnerable hosts in the US and Japan. The vuln is a critical authentication-bypass bug in Rejetto HTTP File Server (HFS) that can lead to full admin access and remote code execution. HFS is an open source web file server that previously appeared on the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities in 2024. On Wednesday, researcher Zach Hanley at AI pen-testing company Horizon3 said he used Mythos to uncover a new flaw in the file server, now tracked as CVE-2026-61500. If you use Rejetto HFS, be sure to update to v3.2.1 or later, which fixes this and other security flaws. Hanley also published a video showing the steps to exploit HFS and remotely execute code on the server. By the next day, the CVE was under exploitation. “We started detecting exploitation of CVE-2026-61500 in Rejetto HFS this evening,” VulnCheck security researcher Patrick Garrity posted on LinkedIn on Thursday, adding that Hanley and team reported the bug to VulnCheck for CVE assignment. “Our canaries detected an actor in China targeting real vulnerable hosts in the US,” Garrity added. Garrity has been tracking CVEs attributed to Mythos and Project Glasswing, Anthropic’s initiative to give select partners access to the bug-hunting model, since shortly after the program was announced in April. Anthropic claims that Mythos is too powerful to release to the general public (insert evil laugh). As of Friday, Mythos and Project Glasswing have uncovered 286 CVEs, according to Garrity’s tracker, and up until Thursday only one of these bugs had been exploited in real-world attacks. The Thursday night activity originated from one IP address in China and targeted vulnerable servers in the US and Japan, Garrity told The Register. “Today we have seen four hits,” he told us on Friday. These originated from two different IP addresses in the US: 173.239.211[.]248 and 173.239.211[.]249. Both are in the same subnet, and “appear to be coming from a proxy,” Garrity added. China-linked digital intruders routinely use compromised devices as proxies to route malicious traffic and disguise the attackers’ true location, and in April a 10-country security advisory warned of China-nexus cyber operatives using proxy networks “strategically, and at scale.” In his write-up, Hanley said Horizon3 has used Mythos in its vulnerability research – and discovered “many critical vulnerabilities” – ever since the security company joined Project Glasswing in July. Mythos' mad math skillz CVE-2026-61500 highlights a couple of Mythos capabilities that make it really good at uncovering vulnerabilities, according to Hanley. Namely, Mythos excels at mathematical distillations and scientific tasks, especially those relating to computer science and operating systems. Finding this CVE “speaks to Mythos’s capabilities in understanding of mathematics, how it identified an exploitable set of cryptographic missteps, and approached solving the constraints to achieve remote code execution,” Hanley wrote. The security issue stems from how HFS authenticates users. It generates a random value with Math.random() and then passes this value to Koa, the Node.js web framework foundation for HFS. Koa uses keygrip to sign all session cookies with that random value. This means that if an “attacker can derive what the session signing key is, they can forge valid session cookies,” Hanley said. This should not be possible, assuming Math.random() uses a secure pseudo random number generator (PRNG). But V8’s Math.random() did not use a secure PRNG. Mythos discovered that the output of the xorshift128+ algorithm it used was fully reversible – and the application was leaking Math.random() outputs. The model’s analysis claimed that Z3, a Microsoft-developed, publicly available Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solver, could be used to recover the PRNG seed. Hanley notes that Horizon3’s researchers could not recall seeing an SMT solver used this way to attack a cryptographic flaw in a real application and bypass authentication. “What makes this impressive is that Mythos didn’t just flag the insecure PRNG in isolation – it simultaneously identified that the application leaked raw Math.random() outputs through a separate code path, recognized those two facts as a chain, and determined the leak produced exactly the observations needed to make state recovery feasible,” he wrote.®

80ad8f3ca40d1015: BACKA TOPOLA: Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has said his side will come out of the international window stronger after two fractious games against Israel that fans and politicians had called on his side to boycott.
The matches had been a focus of attention since the sides were drawn together in February, with Ireland one of Europe's most outspoken critics of Israel's war in Gaza.
There have been numerous protests in Ireland asking for the team not to fulfil the fixtures with Israel.

Such was the opposition to the Irish team playing Israel that the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chose to hold the game behind closed doors in Backa Topola, a small Serbian town of around 12,000 people, rather than in Dublin.

Reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, who declined to be in the squad for the first game against Israel, will again be missing when the two sides meet in Serbia on Sunday, and captain Dara O’Shea will also miss out due to the birth of his child.

“Football-wise, what's to come most of all is to control our focus level and keep the focus on that one (Sunday’s game against Israel), don't lose it,” the Icelandic coach told a press conference on Saturday.
“There's been a lot of emotions from the people in Ireland about this, and obviously that affects the players as well.
"We want to do good, but it's always going to be a challenge when the environment is as noisy as it is,” he said.

Thursday’s 2-2 draw with Austria in Dublin was briefly disrupted by two protests, but a superb goal from Troy Parrott against the Austrians and four points from their last two games have eased the pressure on the Irish team.
The FAI is continuing to investigate allegations that Irish players Adam Idah and James Abankwah were racially abused in Sunday’s 3-0 win over the Israelis in Hungary.
“It just goes to a process both in our departments and then Uefa to look at,” Hallgrimsson said.
“It was something that was reported from both teams. I just hope that we can focus on football and that football will be the winner after this,” he said.
The 59-year-old said the difficulties the team had faced would strengthen them.
“Surviving this camp, coming out of it together as one, would be a massive win for me, that is coming from my heart,” he said.

“I think all the challenges that this team has gone through, all the criticism, yeah, I think just surviving as a group after this game, that will be a big win for me and for this group, (and) for the (football) association," he added.

The news conference ended abruptly when an Israeli journalist asked about an allegation that an Irish player had called an Israeli player "a monkey" during Sunday's game, with Irish press officer Kieran Crowley strongly denying the allegation before quickly bringing it to a close.
0d33f2c514125860: SEPANG: Mercedes driver George Russell has remained optimistic despite his worst grid position of the year for Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix, a week after his brilliant win in Azerbaijan had provided him with a foothold in the world championship race.

Russell's dominant triumph on the streets of Baku shaved 15 points out of championship leader Kimi Antonelli's lead to trim his Mercedes teammate’s title advantage to 66 with a possible 208 still remaining.
But he will start four positions behind his rival on the grid tomorrow, PA Media/dpa reported.

Max Verstappen claimed his first pole of the year and was joined on the front row by Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton, while Isack Hadjar, who qualified third, was relegated five places for taking on new engine parts. His sanction elevated Antonelli to third and Russell to seventh.
Mercedes might have expected their biggest upgrade in four months to propel them further ahead at the sharp end of the pack. Instead, they witnessed their poorest one-lap performance so far.

Their underwhelming grid positions will raise significant questions about the strength of their updates. And Russell will also be pondering his own display. He finished 0.240 seconds adrift of Antonelli despite having one more attempt than his rival in the decisive Q3 running.

However, on the eve of Formula 1’s first fixture in Malaysia since 2017, an optimistic Russell said: “There is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre degradation is huge and, race pace will be king, so even though today was a real disappointment, it is not the be-all and end-all.

“This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac. The lap times nine years ago were six or seven seconds faster, and at certain points, it feels like you are driving on gravel. It’s the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.

“As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us. All the numbers say the upgrade is an improvement but obviously we need to follow the lap times, and not what the numbers say. The numbers look absolutely fine and in line with expectations. However, the result wasn’t.”

The same verdict could not be applied to Verstappen. The Dutch driver was in a class of his own on Saturday and he will be expected to build on his first pole since last December’s finale in Abu Dhabi with his first win of 2026.

Hamilton has endured a disappointing run of late with doubts over the future of Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur lingering in the air. Hamilton is 103 points off the title pace. However, Hamilton converted his last front-row start – at June’s Barcelona Grand Prix – to the sole win of his Ferrari career.

And the 41-year-old, who qualified 0.298 sec adrift of Verstappen, said: “I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much but I guess you talk more when you are happy.
“It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won and I will give it everything tomorrow.”
00e8135a041a681c: GIFU: Coach Brendon Carolan admitted that lax defending led to Malaysia's 5-1 defeat against defending champions India in the Asian Games men's hockey final today.
Consequently, Malaysia missed out on an automatic qualification berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Carolan said poor penalty corner defending was the critical shortcoming in the match.
"Conceding soft penalty corners kind of took the game away from us, and then you have to chase the game because you are goals down," said Carolan.
"PC defence in key moments is hurting us. It almost hurt us against Pakistan, and it hurt us against today."
Malaysia had shown early promise, matching the physical intensity and keeping the game level during the opening 20 minutes.
However, repeated infractions inside the circle handed India numerous set-piece opportunities, unraveling the Speedy Tigers' defensive unit as the match progressed into the second half.
Carolan noted that a gap in match tempo — stemming from a lack of exposure against top-tier world opposition was another major factor in their late-game collapse.
"I thought we were good in the first 20 minutes, and obviously not so good in the last 30–40," he said.
"If you're playing pro league consistently like India are, you're used to playing at a really good tempo. For our guys to play the bigger teams more consistently will help that."
Carolan praised his players for their overall campaign, which included six tough matches and an impressive comeback against Pakistan earlier in the tournament.
He insisted the squad remain motivated as they shift their focus toward the upcoming Olympic qualifying tournaments.
"It would be a disservice to say we're not proud of the guys getting a silver, but if you're a sportsperson, you want to be on top of the podium," Carolan added.
"We feel that we can kick on from here, and it's been a good tournament to set us up for the qualifiers."
The Speedy Tigers will prepare for the Asian Champions Trophy and the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup over the coming months.
7aa583569b508f73: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung has rejected claims that he was absent from PKR affairs for more than a year, saying he became less active after an alleged corporate mafia issue he raised within the party was not acted upon.

Lee, who announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP yesterday, said the claim that he had been "missing for more than a year" from party affairs was inaccurate and diverted attention from the reason for his reduced involvement.
"My statement that I was 'missing for more than a year' from party affairs is inaccurate. It diverts attention from the root cause of this situation.
"I did not distance myself without reason. I became less active after the corporate mafia issue I raised through internal channels was ignored," he said in a Facebook post today.
Yesterday, Lee announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP with immediate effect, following his three-year suspension from PKR.

He said the decision followed his receipt of the suspension decision on Sept 30. He also claimed that access to RM3 million in allocations for the Petaling Jaya constituency had previously been blocked and the funds placed under the management of a party representative.
PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim subsequently said the party had no issue with Lee's resignation, adding that the former MP had not attended PKR meetings or congresses for more than a year.

Lee also questioned PKR's handling of his complaints concerning an alleged corporate mafia, following businessman Victor Chin's allegation that a PKR MP had received RM9.5 million to "settle" a corporate mafia issue involving him.
Lee said such a serious allegation against an elected representative from the ruling party should have been investigated promptly and transparently.
"To this day, no action has been taken. Instead, I, who pushed for the issue to be investigated, was the one who was restricted and punished.
"On Jan 26, I called for an investigation into the issue of excessive shareholdings involving Tan Sri Azam Baki and the corporate mafia issue in Parliament. No action was taken.
"In April, I met the prime minister and sought a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). No action was taken.
"On May 26, my constituency allocation was blocked and handed to a political party to manage. On June 12, I resigned as a member of the PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP).
"On July 2, I received a show-cause letter from the PKR Disciplinary Board. I responded on July 9 but received no reply.
"Then, on Aug 20, I personally wrote to the Disciplinary Board and requested a hearing so that I could defend myself. The request was ignored," he said.
Lee questioned the disciplinary action taken against him after he raised the issues.
"Why was the MP who called for an investigation punished, while the MP accused of receiving RM9.5 million was not investigated?
"Malaysians cannot compromise the country's reputation in the eyes of the international community.
"We cannot be seen as compromising in the fight against corruption, especially under a government elected on a reform mandate," he said.
Lee said the fundamental issue was not who was active or inactive, but why reported misconduct had not been investigated while those who exposed it were punished.
"I remain committed to the people of Petaling Jaya and to the principles that brought me into politics — integrity, accountability and the courage to speak up even when it is unpopular," he said.

e448ca6f5b9764e6: PETALING JAYA: Bekas ketua menteri Sabah yang juga presiden Warisan Shafie Apdal menyokong cadangan konsert penyanyi muzik Kristian Amerika Syarikat (AS), Israel Houghton, di Kota Kinabalu, sambil memetik kebebasan penganut agama itu di Sabah mengamalkan kepercayaan secara aman serta keperluan saling menghormati.
Shafie berkata, konsert berkenaan patut diteruskan tertakluk kelulusan diperlukan dan peraturan yang berkuat kuasa.

"Menyokong kebebasan penganut Kristian di Sabah untuk menghadiri perhimpunan ini tidak bermaksud menyokong setiap pandangan peribadi atau politik yang dipegang oleh artis atau penghibur yang berkunjung," katanya dalam kenyataan beberapa hari selepas polis Sabah membantah penganjuran konsert tersebut.

"Bantahan semata-mata tidak seharusnya menjadi penentu sama ada sesuatu perhimpunan keagamaan boleh diadakan atau tidak. Setiap orang berhak tidak bersetuju dan menyatakan bantahan secara aman. Pada masa sama, mereka yang ingin menghadiri perhimpunan tersebut juga berhak mendapat layanan adil dan dihormati," katanya.

Sokongan beliau terhadap konsert tersebut dibuat tiga hari selepas Bendahari Umno Sabah Salleh Said Keruak, yang juga bekas ketua menteri, menyatakan konsert berkenaan sepatutnya diteruskan, sekiranya masalah keselamatan dapat diuruskan secara munasabah.

Pada Isnin, Pesuruhjaya Polis Sabah Jauteh Dikun, berkata pihak polis akan menasihati kerajaan Sabah supaya menangguhkan konsert Houghton sekiranya penganjur mengemukakan permohonan rasmi. Beliau berkata, nama Houghton serta sokongannya terhadap Israel telah mencetuskan sensitiviti dalam kalangan masyarakat, dengan dua laporan polis telah dibuat atas alasan konsert itu tidak sesuai diadakan masa ini.

Houghton merupakan penyanyi, penulis lagu, dan pemuzik lagu keagamaan serta Kristian kontemporari dari AS, yang juga terkenal menerusi kumpulan Israel & New Breed. Beliau pernah memenangi lapan Anugerah Grammy, termasuk kemenangan terbaharu bagi Album Muzik Kristian Kontemporari Terbaik di Anugerah Grammy 2026.
Shafie berkata, menghormati agama lain termasuk membenarkan orang ramai berkumpul, berdoa, menyanyi, dan menganjurkan program keagamaan mengikut lunas undang-undang.

"Umat Islam, Kristian, Buddha, dan penganut agama lain telah berkongsi bumi ini selama beberapa generasi. Keharmonian beragama kita bergantung kepada usaha memastikan setiap komuniti berasa dihormati dan selamat dalam mengamalkan kepercayaan masing-masing," katanya.

Beliau menyeru pihak berkuasa yang berkaitan memudah cara penganjuran acara ini setelah semua syarat dan keperluan dipenuhi, serta menyeru semua pihak supaya mengamalkan sikap menahan diri dan saling menghormati.
800919b246f5941b: NAGOYA: Chinese football has "a fantastic future" after winning their first Asian Games medal in nearly three decades on Saturday, their men's under-23 coach said.

China beat Uzbekistan on penalties after a 2-2 draw and coach Antonio Puche said he expects the new generation to go on to bigger and better things.
"These players for me have a fantastic future," said the Spaniard.
"We need to work, we need to push them because we have players with big quality and big heart, and this is very important in football."
Asian Games football is under-23 squads that can include three overage players.
Puche's team in Aichi-Nagoya included several players who are regulars with the full national side.
The senior team has struggled in their absence, also going down 3-0 at home to New Zealand in a friendly last week.
Puche backed coach Shao Jiayi to turn things around after the Palestine debacle.
"The result of that last match wasn't very good, that's for sure," he said.
"But the head coach is very capable and resilient and he will use this loss to make the team better."
China have never won Asian Games men's football gold.
They won bronze in 1998 at Bangkok.-AFP

e511b7fd78d9b306: PETALING JAYA: Warisan president Shafie Apdal, a former Sabah chief minister, has backed a proposed concert in Kota Kinabalu by US gospel singer Israel Houghton, citing the freedom of Sabah Christians to practise their faith peacefully and the need for mutual respect.
Shafie said the concert should proceed, subject to the required approvals and applicable rules.

“Supporting the freedom of Sabah’s Christians to attend the concert does not mean supporting every personal or political stance held by the artist or entertainer," he said in a statement days after Sabah police objected to the concert going ahead.

“Objections alone should not determine whether a religious gathering can take place. Everyone has the right to disagree and to express their objections peacefully. At the same time, those who wish to attend also deserve fair treatment and respect,” he said.

His support for the concert comes three days after Sabah Umno treasurer Salleh Said Keruak, also a former chief minister, said the concert should proceed if security concerns could be reasonably managed.

On Monday, Sabah police chief Jauteh Dikun said police would advise the Sabah government to postpone Houghton’s concert if the organisers submitted a formal application. He said Houghton’s name and his support for Israel had triggered sensitivities within the community, with two police reports lodged on the grounds that the concert was unsuitable at this time.

Houghton is a US gospel and contemporary Christian singer, songwriter and musician, also known for the group Israel & New Breed. He has won eight Grammy Awards, including a recent win for Best Contemporary Christian Music Album at the 2026 Grammy Awards.
Shafie said respecting other faiths included allowing people to gather, pray, sing and organise religious programmes within the law.

“Muslims, Christians, Buddhists and those of other religions have shared this land for generations. We must uphold this tradition. Our religious harmony depends on ensuring that every community feels respected and secure in practising its faith,” he said.
He said all security concerns should be addressed and that police should take appropriate measures to maintain public safety and protect those attending.

While his rivals talked about thunderstorms and unpredictable heavy showers at SIC, Red Bull's Verstappen pointed out the heatwave has been really testing the drivers, cars and tyres.
Having won the last Malaysia GP in 2017, Verstappen used his knowledge of the track to good effect by claiming his first pole position of the season on Saturday.
"It's incredible, honestly. I'm very happy to be on pole here. At some tracks, we were kind of close, but now I think this weekend it was very positive for us," said Verstappen.
"It's tough always around here. It's very hot, for ourselves, but also for the cars, for the brakes, for the tyres. So, the race is definitely going to be a tough one.
"You have to manage a lot, and it's impossible to know at the moment, of course, who can do that the best.
"But at the same time, there is a start, where a lot of things can happen. So, we just need to be aware, ready, and then we'll see how competitive we are in the race.
"But so far this weekend, yes, I've felt good, I felt confident, and I hope we can show that again tomorrow."

Verstappen's breakthrough on Saturday means for the first, a non-Mercedes power unit has won pole, with Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, as well as McLaren's Lando Norris and Pierre Gasly, who also use Mercedes engines, the only drivers to have topped the grid previously.
29265fd13ca06476: CHANGLUN: Continuous heavy rain yesterday flooded 27 houses in four villages in Kubang Pasu, with several homes still under water at noon today.

Kubang Pasu Civil Defence Force officer Mohd Adenin Suhaimi said that as of 11.25am, eight houses each in Kampung Changkat Sentol and Kampung Belukar were affected, along with six in Kampung Sungai Petani and five in Kampung Padang, according to BuletinTV3.
"However, no temporary evacuation centre has been opened so far. All affected heads of households have left and are staying at homestays or with relatives nearby," he said in a statement.
Roads temporarily closed this morning were understood to have reopened after the water receded, while most residents had begun cleaning their homes.
A check at 1pm found several houses in Kampung Sungai Petani and Kampung Belukar remained flooded despite water levels in surrounding areas subsiding.
The houses are located lower than the road, causing water to remain trapped inside, with levels in some homes reaching calf height.
For Kampung Belukar resident Aishah Ahmad, 78, flooding has been an annual ordeal throughout her 60 years living in the area.
She said just a day of heavy rain was enough to send water into her home, making it difficult to deal with the aftermath.
"I have lived here for 60 years, and every year the water rises here. Heavy rain for just about a day and it floods immediately.
"I am tired. When this happens, I can't do anything. I have no energy. Water entered my house up to two steps high," she said when met at Kampung Belukar today.
Another resident, Mohammad Irsyadi Darus, 37, said the water rose to knee level before receding within about an hour.
He said past experience had taught residents to stay prepared by moving their belongings to higher ground to minimise losses should the water return.
"The water rose to knee level but within an hour it had receded. Usually, if there is heavy rain for two to three hours, the water will rise, which is why we are cautious.
"Even now, we have placed our belongings in high places, afraid a second wave of floods will come," he said.
Civil Defence Force monitoring showed water levels at Sungai Batu 15 Sintok, Sungai Sintok, Sungai Badak and Sungai Tok Kassim were on a downward trend.
